title: No Measurable Benefit from Verifier‑Assisted Generate→Validate→Repair under Shared‑Initial Generation: A Preregistered Emulation Study
abstract: We preregistered and autonomously executed a paired emulation study (study-cnd-2026-001) to test whether a verifier‑assisted generate→validate→repair pipeline increases oracle pass rates for LLM‑generated network configurations in emulated intent→configuration NetOps tasks. The frozen design used shared_initial_candidate generation semantics with a single generator call per pair, declared model gpt-5-mini, a deterministic validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5), and a repair budget ≤1 call/task. Execution produced 200 paired units (400 episodes); model_calls_used=200 and repair calls invoked=0. Results: baseline 200/200 oracle passes; guarded 200/200 oracle passes; paired difference = 0.00 (paired bootstrap 95% CI [0.00,0.00], bootstrap_resamples=10000, seed=1729); exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.00. The null outcome is design‑bound: the shared_initial_candidate semantics produced identical passing candidates for both arms so repairs were never exercised. We release the full audited artifact bundle and give artifact‑grounded recommendations (independent generation, calibrated difficulty, larger repair budgets) to generate informative contrasts in future runs.

sections.introduction: Generative LLMs are being explored to translate high‑level NetOps intent into vendor CLI sequences or device changes. Operational safety requires objective verification (reachability, protected interfaces, make‑before‑break). A common architecture is generate→validate→repair: a generator proposes a configuration candidate, a deterministic validator verifies safety/policy predicates in an emulated model, and a repair module attempts corrective regeneration if the oracle fails. Prior reports show promise for verifier assistance, but reproducible, preregistered, artifact‑anchored evaluations are rare. We preregistered study‑cnd‑2026‑001 to provide a strictly frozen, fully archived, paired comparison. The preregistration (SHA‑256 a8969ac01f3b1bb7...) fixed the estimand, task bank, generation semantics (shared_initial_candidate), model (gpt‑5‑mini), validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5), repair budget, stopping rules, and analysis executor. All raw outputs, provider traces, validator traces, and per‑file SHA‑256 digests were archived for deterministic audit.
sections.related_work: LLM‑driven NetOps research spans intent translation, constrained generation, verifier‑augmented pipelines, and repair loops. Notable lines include constraint‑guided generators (e.g., MeshAgent), intent→configuration benchmarks (NetConfEval), and verifier‑grounded repair architectures (verifier→counterexample→repair). Work on verifier‑grounded program repair (e.g., StruSpec) emphasizes executing validators to return precise counterexamples for targeted repair. Our contribution differs: we preregistered a confirmatory paired run, executed it under immutable semantics, and publish the complete artifact trail (generation traces, validator traces, scoring JSON, execution manifest, and SHA‑256 digests) to make the design consequences auditable.
sections.methodology: Preregistration and frozen design: The preregistered plan (study id = study-cnd-2026-001; SHA‑256 a8969ac01f3b...) froze the primary estimand paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline, stratified 200 paired tasks across four protocol buckets (BGP/OSPF/ACL/VLAN = 50 each), vendor allocation (Cisco 68 / Juniper 68 / Arista 64), and complexity (simple=100, complex=100). Generation semantics = shared_initial_candidate (one generated candidate per pair supplied identically to both baseline and guarded conditions), declared model = gpt-5-mini (execution/model_configuration.json SHA‑256 1acce92558ed...), deterministic validator = deterministic_netops_validator_v5, maximum_repair_calls_per_task = 1, and analysis executor = paired_binary_analysis_v1 with paired bootstrap percentile CI (10,000 resamples, seed=1729). The frozen initial master prompt that launched the autonomous post‑lock research run is archived at provenance/master_prompt.txt (SHA‑256 1872df1e1805d2d9...).
sections.results: Execution summary (artifact‑backed): The autonomous run completed per preregistration: planned_episode_count=400, completed_episode_count=400, failed_episode_count=0, model_calls_used=200. Scoring artifacts (execution/scoring/*.json) show every shared candidate passed the deterministic validator. Confirmatory contingency (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv SHA‑256 7bc1bd2a...): n11=200, n10=0, n01=0, n00=0. Numeric inference (paired_binary_analysis_v1): baseline_success_rate = 200/200 = 1.0; guarded_success_rate = 200/200 = 1.0; paired difference = 0.00; paired bootstrap 95% percentile CI = [0.00, 0.00] (bootstrap_resamples=10000, seed=1729); exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.00. Repair activity: repair_applied=false for all episodes and no repair provider traces were generated (repair_calls_invoked = 0). Representative scoring traces are archived (e.g., execution/scoring/task-000001-baseline.json SHA‑256 eaf96aec12c3...).
sections.discussion:
Why the null outcome occurred: Under the preregistered shared_initial_candidate semantics the generator produced a single candidate per pair which was delivered identically to baseline and guarded arms. The deterministic validator accepted every shared candidate across the 200 pairs; therefore the repair stage had no opportunity to act and the paired contrast is uninformative about repair efficacy. This is an auditable, design‑bound explanation supported by provider call traces and scoring artifacts (see execution/provider_calls/* and execution/scoring/* JSON files and their SHA‑256 digests recorded in execution/execution_manifest.json).

Implications and recommended next steps (artifact‑anchored): The null result does not dismiss verifier assistance generally; it exposes a necessary alignment condition: the generation semantics and task difficulty must allow validator failures for repair to matter. Two directly reproducible, low‑risk variants (use the archived prompts and seeds): (1) independent_generation semantics — generate independent candidates per condition per pair (expected model_calls≈400) so baseline and guarded arms sample distinct generator randomness; (2) calibrated difficulty/adversarialization — add tasks or alter required_sequence constraints so a meaningful fraction of generator candidates fail the validator. Also increase maximum_repair_calls_per_task (≥2) to permit iterative repair loops. All suggested variants reuse the same validator and analysis executor and are executable within the archived adapter framework; the artifact bundle documents exact paths and hashes for deterministic re‑runs.

Threats to validity: Internal validity is dominated by prompt/generation semantics sensitivity (explicit and preregistered, logged in model_configuration.json and provider traces). Construct validity: the deterministic validator enforces a set of emulation‑based predicates but may not capture all production failure modes; validator traces include parsed counts and violation lists to support oracle coverage inspection. External validity: single declared model (gpt‑5‑mini) and emulated tasks limit generality; reproduction across other models and production device images is required before operational claims. Conclusion validity: the paired analysis is correct for the observed contingency; the degenerate concordant outcome yields a precise zero CI which truthfully reflects the preregistered estimand under the frozen design.
sections.conclusion: We preregistered and executed an auditable paired emulation run to test verifier‑assisted generate→validate→repair. Under the exact frozen design (shared_initial_candidate semantics, gpt‑5‑mini, deterministic validator, repair budget ≤1), verifier assistance produced no measurable benefit because the single shared generated candidate per pair passed the oracle for every task and repairs were never invoked (repair_calls_invoked=0). The complete artifact trail (generation, provider traces, scoring JSON, execution manifest, per‑file SHA‑256 digests) is released to enable deterministic replication and immediate follow‑ups that modify generation semantics or task difficulty to produce informative contrasts.

disclosure_statement:

The preregistration froze the primary hypothesis, sampling plan, generation semantics (shared_initial_candidate), declared model, validator, repair budget, stopping rules, and analysis executor.

All provider call traces and raw responses are archived under execution/provider_calls/ and execution/responses/ with per‑file SHA‑256 digests recorded in execution/execution_manifest.json.
- Generation semantics (frozen): shared_initial_candidate — one generator call per pair whose produced candidate was provided identically to both baseline and guarded conditions. This preregistered choice produced model_calls_used=200 (one shared generation per 200 pairs) and is the proximate cause the guarded repair stage was never invoked (repair_calls_invoked = 0). See execution/execution_manifest.json for counts and per‑file hashes.
- Validator and oracle: deterministic_netops_validator_v5 scored every candidate; representative scoring artifact: execution/scoring/task-000001-baseline.json (SHA‑256 = eaf96aec12c30860...). All validator traces and scoring JSON files are archived and hashed.
- Repair policy and budget: preregistered maximum_repair_calls_per_task = 1; in this run repair calls invoked = 0 (artifact‑backed). Repair prompts and repair provider traces would be archived if invoked.
- Analysis procedures (frozen): paired_binary_analysis_v1; paired bootstrap 10,000 resamples (seed=1729) and exact McNemar two‑sided test. Confirmatory analysis artifacts: analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv (SHA‑256 = 7bc1bd2a42b5...) and analysis/condition_summary.csv (SHA‑256 = 1cb072b4db7c...).
- Execution reproducibility: every prompt, model output, provider trace, validator trace, scoring record, manifest and analysis artifact is archived with SHA‑256 digests in execution/execution_manifest.json. Deterministic reconciliation confirms accounting consistency (analysis/deterministic_reconciliation.json SHA‑256 = 799b23b993fcc9c04...).
- Human involvement: Pre‑lock collaborative development and approval of the master prompt were performed by the Research Director. No human performed manual substantive editing of the manuscript after the autonomy lock. Pre‑lock development artifacts were not used as empirical evidence unless reproduced under the frozen post‑lock workflow.
- Deviations: none affecting the primary confirmatory analysis; the declared model did not change mid‑run; no pairs were excluded; repairs were not triggered. Full execution manifest and per‑file SHA‑256 digests are provided in the artifact bundle for audit.
limitations: Conclusions apply only to the exact preregistered design (shared_initial_candidate semantics, gpt-5-mini, deterministic_netops_validator_v5, synthetic/emulated task bank of 200).

Shared_initial_candidate semantics produced a ceiling effect: a single shared generated candidate per pair passed the oracle in every case so the repair stage was never invoked (repair_calls_invoked = 0), preventing measurement of guarded repair efficacy in this run.

Emulation with a deterministic validator and synthetic tasks does not capture production heterogeneity (real vendor images, run‑time nondeterminism, device‑specific quirks); external validity is therefore limited.
Single‑model execution limits generality across model families and instruction‑tuning variants; replication across models is required for broader claims.
Repair budget was intentionally limited (≤1 call/task) by preregistration; richer iterative repair policies remain unexplored and may be necessary to observe repair convergence.
Oracle blind spots remain possible; validator coverage diagnostics are archived but definitive coverage of all semantic failure modes cannot be guaranteed from emulation alone.
